script: Spread and total were not saved for CIN at MIA, so this is form-only: the Cincinnati Bengals' weeks 2-4 were pass-driven by Tee Higgins (33 targets, 342 yards, 404 air yards) with Chase Brown at 42 carries for 151, while the Miami Dolphins' weeks 2-4 were run-led by Ollie Gordon (29 carries, 148 yards) and Malik Willis (13 carries, 73 yards). Without a number, the CIN@MIA lean is Cincinnati throwing and Miami handing Gordon the ball into a Bengals defense that has allowed 4.86 yards per carry.
who_goes_off: In CIN at MIA, Tee Higgins is the Cincinnati Bengals skill player set to go off, 114 receiving yards per game on 11 targets versus Ja'Marr Chase at 66.7 on 8 targets, and Ollie Gordon is the Miami Dolphins back to produce, 49.3 rush yards per game at 5.1 yards per carry. Chase Brown's 50.3 Bengals rush yards per game does not support a ceiling game against Miami's 4.01 yards per carry allowed.
weak_spot: In this CIN@MIA game both pass defenses leak in the middle, not outside: the Miami Dolphins have allowed 9.66 yards per attempt on 32 middle throws versus 7.66 left (41 attempts) and 7.92 right (40), and the Cincinnati Bengals have allowed 9.91 on 34 middle throws versus 6.53 on the right (58 attempts). Cincinnati's structural hole versus Miami is the run at 4.86 yards per carry and 11 runs of 10-plus, while Miami's run defense versus the Bengals is tighter at 4.01 yards per carry.
injury_fallout: No injury designations were saved for CIN at MIA, so nothing moves Cincinnati's Tee Higgins off 33 targets, Bengals back Chase Brown off 42 carries, or Miami's Ollie Gordon off 29 carries from the last three games.
qb_vs_blitz: Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow is -0.13 EPA per dropback versus the blitz on 46 dropbacks and +0.21 when the Miami Dolphins do not blitz, and MIA's blitz rate is 29%, so nearly a third of CIN dropbacks are the worse split. Miami's quarterback is -0.34 EPA versus the blitz on 45 dropbacks and only +0.01 unblitzed, but the Bengals blitz just 16%, so MIA mostly sees the cleaner look and can stay with Gordon.

picks.why: Cincinnati Bengals receiver Tee Higgins has 342 receiving yards on 33 targets and 404 air yards over the last three games, about 114 yards a game, against a 51.5 line, and the Miami Dolphins' middle has allowed 9.66 yards per attempt on 32 throws. Even a hard cut from 114 in this CIN@MIA game still clears 51.5 unless MIA's 29% blitz fully erases that Bengals target share.

Cincinnati Bengals back Chase Brown has 151 rush yards on 42 carries the last three games, 50.3 per game at 3.60 yards per carry, and the CIN rush line is 64.5. The Miami Dolphins have allowed 4.01 yards per carry, which on his 14-carry pace is about 56 yards, still under 64.5, and Higgins' 33 targets plus Ja'Marr Chase's 24 do not point to an 18-carry Brown game in MIA.
